segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ יוֹצְאִין בְּבֵיצַת הַחַרְגּוֹל וּבְשֵׁן שׁוּעָל וּבְמַסְמֵר מִן הַצָּלוּב, מִשּׁוּם רְפוּאָה — דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין אַף בַּחוֹל, מִשּׁוּם דַּרְכֵי הָאֱמוֹרִי.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «One may go out» on Shabbat «with a locust egg, and with a fox tooth, and with a nail from the crucified, for» the purpose of «healing;» this is «the statement of Rabbi Meir. The Rabbis prohibit» using these remedies «even during the week, due to the» prohibition of following the «ways of the Amorite.» These are superstitious beliefs and the customs of gentiles from which one must distance oneself.

moves.summary: R' Meir permits going out with these remedies
the Sages forbid them even on weekdays as Amorite ways

edges.about: whether one may use a locust egg, fox tooth or crucifixion nail as a remedy (R' Meir: yes, even on Shabbat; Sages: forbidden even on weekdays as Amorite ways)

positions.claim: one may go out with them on Shabbat for healing
